entries.agent_impact: A consumer may now read a declarative, schema-validated description of how a checkout at a resolved commit becomes a usable installed runtime, and enforce it: exact commands, accepted Node and npm ranges, per-step network policy, the enumerated input set, seven mandatory output checks, and five bounds. It is data only — this repository publishes the recipe and executes no step of it. Enforcement is fail-closed: an unrecognized recipe kind, revision, or safety-critical enum is refused, and a check that cannot be performed counts as failed rather than skipped. Two readings a consumer must not take: the input set is the compiler's resolved file list rather than its configured globs, and campaign-spec/dist is a build output with no committed baseline, so output verification is self-consistency rather than comparison against a hash published here. A prepared generation can build and type-check but cannot run browser QA. Nothing existing changed shape; adoption is optional and additive.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-kind.json. recipe_kind names a kind this schema version does not define. An installed consumer was not released knowing how to execute it, so it fails closed rather than guessing that a v2 is a v1 with extras.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-revision.json. recipe_revision leaves the major line the kind defines. A revision may only re-parameterise fields the consumer already understands; a different major is a shape change wearing a revision's clothes.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-network-policy.json. A safety-critical enum: the install step declares a network policy outside the defined set. There is no allow-all value, and an unrecognized one is refused rather than treated as permissive.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/allowlist-without-hosts.json. An allowlist with no hosts is not a bound, it is an empty declaration that reads like one. The schema requires a non-empty host list whenever the policy is an allowlist.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-output-check.json. A safety-critical enum: an output check names a kind the consumer cannot perform. A new KIND of check is a new recipe kind, because an installed consumer cannot perform a check it was not released knowing.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-step-id.json. A safety-critical enum: a step identity outside the defined set. Steps are identified rather than positional, so an unrecognized id is a command the consumer has no contract for.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/lifecycle-scripts-enabled.json. A safety-critical enum: a step that permits lifecycle scripts. Enabling them would let the target run arbitrary code during preparation, which is the single thing the recipe's flags exist to prevent.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/engines-disagreement-warns.json. A safety-critical enum: disagreement between the contract's tool range and the target's declared engines resolved as a warning. An accept-with-warning path produces a build made under conditions nobody approved.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/advisory-enforcement.json. fail_closed switched off. Advisory bounds record the right numbers and enforce nothing, so the first time a bound matters you discover it was decorative.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unperformable-check-skipped.json. A safety-critical enum: a check that cannot be performed treated as skipped. A skipped check reports success it never established.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/committed-output-claim.json. The recipe claims its output directory is a committed artifact. It is not: the directory is git-ignored and untracked, so no baseline for its contents can exist here and verification must be self-consistency.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unpinned-lockfile.json. The recipe claims its lockfile is not integrity-pinned. The network allowlist bounds where bytes may come from and the lockfile's digests bound which bytes are acceptable; dropping the second leaves the first standing alone, which it was never meant to do.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/missing-required-field.json. The enumerated input set is absent. Without it there is nothing to fingerprint, and staleness — the one failure mode no output-side check can see — becomes undetectable.

The one script a recipe build step is meant to run. Not a tripwire: it logs to its own file so "the intended script ran" and "nothing else ran" stay separable, and a fixture that only proved emptiness cannot pass by never building at all.

entries.agent_impact: A fourth checkpoint gate is registered, built_output.upsell_selector_scope, and it can block a doctor run that previously passed. It fires when a built page whose funnel role is upsell or downsell carries a data-next-bundle-selector that lacks data-next-upsell-context and is in the default swap selection mode: such a selector writes to the shopper's live cart at init, so loading the page charges them for a package at the next checkout without it appearing in that checkout's rendered order summary. Two consequences a consumer must plan for. First, `doctor --built` can now return blocked; it previously only produced warnings, and a consumer treating that mode as advisory will need to read its exit state. Second, all eight certified template families (apollo, apollo-mv-single-step, demeter, olympus, olympus-mv-single-step, olympus-mv-two-step, shop-single-step, shop-three-step) currently ship a display-only selector with neither attribute across 19 upsell offer includes, so a campaign built from any certified family blocks until the templates are repaired upstream in campaign-cart-starter-templates. The remedy is to add data-next-upsell-context to the named selector, or to record a bounded named-human waiver through `campaigns-os checkpoint waive --gate built_output.upsell_selector_scope`. data-next-selection-mode="select" also clears the blocker and reports a warning instead, because the SDK gates every cart write on swap mode.

entries.agent_impact: Two `qa resolve` outputs that could be believed no longer can be. First, `status: ready` now asserts that the derived entry URLs were probed AND resolved; it previously asserted only that they were derived from the packet, so a route set that was 100% dead reported ready with a next command that could not succeed. A consumer reading resolve status must handle two new terminal values: `routes_unresolved` (probed, at least one route dead, `ok: false`, first failing URL named, `qa run` suggestion suppressed) and `ready_unprobed` (routes existed but none produced a response, `ok: true`). Both are additive; the existing three values keep their meaning over probed-and-resolved routes. The status ladder is ordered by verification coverage, so `ready_unprobed` outranks `ready_with_exceptions` — read `checkpoint_gates[]` for warnings rather than inferring them from status. Offline and CI runs need no flag: a transport error degrades to `ready_unprobed` rather than failing, because a 404 is evidence about the deployment while a transport error is evidence about the caller network. `--no-probe` is for hermetic runs that must make no outbound request. Second, `theme_gate.no_commerce_pages` no longer fires on a campaign whose declared funnel includes commerce pages that this build left out of scope, so a consumer that treated that code as proof of a content-only campaign was reading a build-scope artifact. Theme gate results gain `commerce_pages_out_of_scope`, and `scope_source` gains `doctor_derived_scope+spec_topologies`. Resolve remains a diagnostic command and still exits 0 on every status.

changes.summary: `qa resolve` gained --no-probe and --probe-timeout-ms, and two terminal statuses, routes_unresolved and ready_unprobed, alongside the existing ready / ready_with_exceptions / blocked. Probing the derived entry URLs is the default; --no-probe is for hermetic runs that must make no outbound request, since an offline run already degrades to ready_unprobed without it.

The Resolve section now documents route reachability: the full status ladder and why it is ordered by verification coverage, the five route_probe reason codes, the offline/CI degradation rule that separates an HTTP 404 from a transport error, the 25-URL probe cap, and the two route-root diagnoses emitted when every derived route is dead. It also records that resolve exits 0 on every status, routes_unresolved included.

The Theme Gate section now states that "ships commerce pages" is a property of the campaign rather than of one build: the gate reads built pages plus declared commerce pages this build left out of scope, the QA path unions the declared funnel into the doctor-derived scope, and commerce_pages_out_of_scope and the scope_source values are named.

entries.agent_impact: Browser QA now emits assertions for two things it previously said nothing about, and both can newly block a verdict that used to pass. A checkout page whose CampaignSpec declares exit_intent or promo_code_input with enabled: true gets browser-exit-intent-surface:<page> / browser-promo-code-surface:<page>: absent markup is FAIL/BLOCKER, markup carrying the declared offer_code is PASS, markup that cannot be tied to that code (or a coupon input behind an unopened disclosure) is MANUAL_REVIEW/WARN, and a browser collector that threw mid-read is SKIPPED with the cause rather than blocking. Typed-card runs additionally emit browser-order-display-parity:<plan> and browser-order-total-parity:<plan>, reconciling the persisted order pre-upsell read-back against what the checkout displayed at submit; a non-upsell line whose package was never rendered as selected, a displayed package that was never charged, or a total that disagrees with the displayed summary total is FAIL/BLOCKER naming the package ids. Both reconciliation assertions report SKIPPED with a stated reason when the page gives them nothing comparable - a summary whose rows do not all carry data-package-id, or a checkout with no [data-next-display="cart.total"] surface - and a consumer must read that as missing coverage, never as a pass. Both sets reuse the existing browser-runtime and browser-test-order families, so the verdict schema, QA_ASSERTION_FAMILY_VOCABULARY, and any allowlist keyed off it are unchanged. A campaign that declares a surface it did not build, or charges a package it never displayed, will now block where it previously reported ready.

entries.agent_impact: The runtime recipe now states the guarantee its network policy actually makes. No declared field changed — install remains allowlist against registry.npmjs.org, build remains deny, the cache remains consumer-owned, and inherited proxy/credential/npmrc configuration is still refused — so an existing consumer's behaviour is unchanged and no action is required. The prose previously invited reading 'allowlist' as a host-level network sandbox; it is a package-manager configuration bound, and what prevents third-party code from disregarding it is --ignore-scripts on both steps, not the network layer. A consumer that added a real sandbox on the strength of the old wording remains correct and is now explicitly encouraged; a consumer that treated the hosts as advisory was already in violation and still is.

An outcome the runner cannot prove either way stops the path and names an operator check instead of resubmitting. A spent slot with no confirmed order is the ambiguous case, not an order to reconcile. Read evidence.recovery to tell a recovered pass from a first-attempt pass. New flag qa run --max-order-creations <n>, defaulting to the planned path count and refused wherever a browser path builds its creation budget (qa run and qa parity alike) when it is non-numeric, fractional, negative or zero; --max-test-orders keeps its existing meaning.

entries.agent_impact: The run-record closeout command qa run prints as "Required next" carries --no-remit whenever the attempt does not end the run session - a BLOCKED verdict, or any disposition this version does not recognise - and says why. Such an attempt keeps the run session open, so an agent executing the printed command verbatim no longer spends the session run_id on the interim record; the session close (the later ready auto-end, or run end) is then the first and only POST for that id and lands remit_state ok instead of failed. A session-ending verdict is unchanged: it auto-ends the session in the same process, before the printed command can run, so the command mints its own run_id and remits, exactly as it does with no session. An agent that pattern-matches the closeout command string must accept an optional --no-remit between --qa-verdict and --json. Separately, an auto-end whose own remit does not close now says so on stderr and names the local record to keep; it does not print a re-send command, because run-record --run-id reassembles from current disk state rather than reloading the written record, and a session s QA attempt references are gone once the session is cleared - on a run repaired across several attempts that command replaces the stored record with a thinner one and sends that. The same caveat is now stated beside the run_record_remit_recovery action an agent may already be following. Re-sending a persisted record is not implemented. Remit itself is unchanged on the wire - the docs that called the endpoint an upsert now state that it keeps one record per run_id and refuses a repeat POST for a stored id with 409, so retrying a send that failed is safe and re-sending one that succeeded is not. Which dispositions end a session is one exported set, SESSION_ENDING_DISPOSITIONS, read by both the auto-end and the closeout it prints; membership is enumerated rather than excluded, so a disposition from a newer or foreign verdict keeps the session open on both sides instead of leaving them to disagree over who owns the run_id.

entries.agent_impact: `next` gains one non-required advisory action, theme_gate.starter_palette_blocks_qa, in next_actions[] at the build, polish, deploy and qa stages. It is emitted when the theme gate's code is theme_gate.nothing_generatable (no brand tokens, nothing generated, gate passes) AND the packet's assembly.template_family resolves to a brand contract carrying both forbidden computed colors and commerce selectors to inspect them on — the same predicate the browser runner uses to decide whether template-residue:<page>:style:* rows are produced at all. It says browser QA will block on the starter palette and names the two lanes that clear it: `campaigns-os theme waive` (downgrades those rows to warn severity) or a hand-authored brand-theme.css loaded after next-core.css. A family outside the certified set (custom, undecided, or any family with no contract) produces no palette rows, so it is not warned. The non-JSON tiny prompt prints the same warning alongside, not instead of, the stage's existing prompt. No gate status, severity, or exit code changes, and nothing is waived automatically; a waived or applied gate emits nothing. A second non-required action, theme_gate.brand_contract_unreadable, appears at the same stages when the family's brand contract exists but fails to load (parse_error, schema_mismatch, extends_cycle, extends_missing_parent, family_mismatch): it names the family and the error code and says browser QA rejects such a contract outright as a template-brand-contract:<family> blocker that no waiver clears. That one does not depend on the theme gate outcome, because QA rejects the contract whether or not the campaign has brand tokens; a family that simply resolves to no contract is not a defect and emits nothing. next still never throws over a defective contract. Every value interpolated into that advisory is bounded before it is printed or serialized: the family must match the lowercase template-family slug or it reads unknown-family, the code must be one of the loader's own or it reads unknown, and the loader detail is folded to one trimmed line with control characters stripped, Markdown escaped, and length capped; the repair path names contracts/template-brand-contract.<family>.v0.json only when that file is on disk and otherwise names the private fragment supplying it. A consumer that treats every next_actions[] entry as a command to execute must read `command: null` / absent `required` as advisory, as it already must for purchase_proof_unknown and run_record_present.
entries.migration: none. Consumers keying on action ids may add theme_gate.starter_palette_blocks_qa; ignoring it leaves previous behaviour unchanged.

changes.summary: next emits a non-required theme_gate.starter_palette_blocks_qa action at build/polish/deploy/qa when the theme gate passes with code theme_gate.nothing_generatable, no waiver is recorded, and the packet's template family has applicable palette-residue checks, naming the QA consequence and both clearing lanes; a defective (unreadable) brand contract emits theme_gate.brand_contract_unreadable instead, naming the family and the loader's error code, independently of the theme gate; the tiny prompt is split into an assertable line builder and prints the same warning without displacing the stage prompt.

States the token-less rule in the theme section: the gate passes with nothing to generate, browser QA then blocks on the starter palette at blocker severity, and the waiver or a hand-authored brand layer is the bypass.

entries.agent_impact: QA and doctor findings now carry a cause class, so a consumer can tell whether the change under test caused what a run surfaced instead of re-reading every finding by hand. Two additive optional fields ride each finding: cause (caused_by_change | pre_existing | test_environment | upstream_drift | unknown) and cause_reason (a short reason code). A cause_summary object ({surface, total, counts, prior_run_id, comparison}, plus prior_qa_attempt_run_id on the QA side) rides the QA verdict and the doctor output; prior_run_id is the previous Run Record's id on both surfaces, and the QA summary additionally names the final attempt within that record it read. The fields appear on the full verdict, on the derived exceptions, on the committed QA verdict sidecar, and on every doctor result — classification is applied where the doctor result is produced, so all four producers that persist .campaign-runtime/doctor-output.json leave the labels on the retained artifact. Passing assertions carry none, and non-packet doctor (--built / --site) is not annotated. Absence is not a claim: output emitted before this release carries neither field, and the first run on a campaign labels every finding unknown because there is no earlier run to compare against. The human reports gained a summary line and a per-finding tag; the doctor issue line keeps its existing "[code] message" shape with the tag appended.
entries.migration: none. Tolerate cause/cause_reason/cause_summary being absent, and never read an absent cause_summary as "nothing was caused by the change". A consumer that wants the labels to be meaningful must let campaigns-os run-record write a Run Record after each run, since the previous run is found through Run Record discovery.

changes.summary: Every doctor result is stamped with cause and cause_reason per error and warning plus a cause_summary, applied where the result is produced rather than in the doctor command, so the retained doctor artifact keeps its labels whichever producer wrote it last. The comparison is against the previous Run Record's doctor code observations. The doctor human report prints the summary line and appends a cause tag to each issue line. The run-record discovery helpers moved to src/run-record.mjs and are re-exported here unchanged.

Documents the cause-class vocabulary, the single previous-run comparison rule (including that QA compares against the prior run's last, final QA attempt) and its fingerprints, every unknown reason code including the first-run case, and where the labels appear across the verdict, the exceptions, the committed sidecar and every doctor producer.

entries.agent_impact: The document-wrapper policy is now selectable before the build stage. source-html-manifest/v0 accepts an optional top-level wrapper_policy key (strip_document_wrappers, preserve_document_wrappers, not_required, unknown), and prepare-build / start / build accept a --wrapper-policy flag in the same vocabulary; prepare-build seeds source_html.adapter_contract.wrapper_policy from the resolved value, so a selected preserve_document_wrappers reports source_html.prep.document_wrapper as a warning instead of blocking. Precedence is flag, then manifest key, then the unchanged default strip_document_wrappers. A manifest wrapper_policy outside the vocabulary does not invalidate the manifest: the key is ignored with a warning naming it, the value, and the accepted values, and pages[], producer_provenance, and files[] are used as written. An unrecognized or valueless flag refuses the run before prepare-build writes anything, so a bad argument strands no Design Source Package.
entries.migration: none. A run that passes no flag and a manifest carrying no wrapper_policy key behaves exactly as before.

changes.summary: Declares the optional top-level wrapper_policy key with the adapter contract's four-value enum, naming the flag override, the default, and the non-fatal handling of an out-of-enum value.

Adds --wrapper-policy to prepare-build (and to start / build, which run the same prepare step): validates the flag with the other up-front argv checks so a bad value refuses before any output is written, resolves flag over manifest key over default, seeds the packet's adapter contract from the result, and echoes a non-default selection and any non-fatal manifest warning with its channel on stderr.

entries.agent_impact: No behaviour change. On DESIGN_SOURCE_PACKAGE_NOT_READY for a template-stock page, the available route now depends on the template family. If the family's catalog entry publishes a complete Template Reference (today apollo alone), declare the template-derived pages out of source scope — a per-page skip_reason manifest entry, or build_scope.mode "partial" — and synthesis emits template_baseline coverage for them; intake clears as a partial build, so prepare_build ends completed_partial, the pages sit under declared_out_of_scope and derived.scope, only mapped routes are previewable, and checkout launch and test-order proof stay blocked. For any other family there is no template_baseline to synthesize and no operator channel; by policy none is coming in v0, and the page is build-stage work for next-campaigns-build. In neither case is attesting a screenshot of stock template output acceptable.

entries.agent_impact: campaigns-os doctor no longer rewrites the Assembly Report when its restated outcome matches what stages.doctor already carries, ignoring only that stage's checked_at and completed_at. A Run Record's assembly_report sha256 therefore keeps verifying across repeated doctor runs that reach the same outcome; a changed outcome still rewrites the report and breaks the digest, which is the attestation working. doctor-output.json is still refreshed on every run. stages.doctor.checked_at now reads as the time the current outcome was last established, not the time doctor last ran. The stage ledger exports producerStageOutcomeUnchanged(previousReport, nextReport, stage).

entries.agent_impact: Four documented facts a consumer may have been getting wrong, with no behaviour change behind them. First, a checkpoint gate's status is the blocking axis only: page_kit.store_profile returns status pass with code page_kit.store_profile.target_only and the affected fields in warning_fields[] when the target declares a governed Store Profile field the CampaignSpec leaves empty, and qa resolve chooses between ready and ready_with_exceptions from warning_fields[] (or an active waiver), not from status — so read code and warning_fields[], never status alone, to decide whether a gate is clean. Second, sequence is the authoritative order of contracts/release-ledger.json (it is the entry's position in entries[], and the gate derives the expected value from that position) while id is an immutable label that is never reused or renumbered; the two diverge legitimately when concurrent pull requests restamp sequence on merge, so order by sequence and identify by id and infer neither from the other. Third, a change that lives entirely in policy-ignored paths carries a same-surface CHANGELOG section and no ledger entry, because every change item must map to a classified changed path in the range; any src/cli.mjs change is cli_surface and owes an entry. Fourth, Design Source Package intake only reads under the source root and writes every artifact under the target repository, and a screenshots[] record is available with a url as well as a path, so the readiness gate can clear against a source root the operator cannot write and with no capture bytes in the source tree; the manifest path is fixed and source_html.root is stored relative to the packet, so a packet resolves its source from where it was written.

changes.summary: The checkpoint-preflight section now states that a gate's status is the blocking axis only: a pass can carry non-blocking findings in warning_fields[] (page_kit.store_profile.target_only), which is what qa resolve and the packet QA assertion read.

Adds the sequence-versus-id rule (position is the authoritative order; ids are never renumbered and may diverge after concurrent merges) and a subsection recording that a fix confined to policy-ignored paths carries a CHANGELOG section and no ledger entry, while any src/cli.mjs change owes one.
New generated section "Ledger order and entry identity" states that sequence is the authoritative ledger order and id is an immutable label that may legitimately diverge from it.

Documents the read-only source root: intake reads under the source root and writes its artifacts under the target repository, url-only screenshot records satisfy desktop/mobile proof, and the fixed manifest path plus the packet-relative source_html.root are the mechanics to plan around.

entries.agent_impact: start / prepare-build / build now report the template-family precedence they always applied. When --template-family and the CampaignSpec preferred_template_family hint name different families, the flag still wins (packet.assembly.template_family and template_lock are unchanged), but the run prints one stderr line naming both values and their channels, and the assembly report's warnings[] gains an advisory entry { code: "TEMPLATE_FAMILY_HINT_OVERRIDDEN", stage: "prepare_build", message } naming the winning flag and the overridden hint. A flag equal to the hint, a hint with no flag, and a flag with no hint all stay silent. No exit code, blocker, or gate changes; an agent that ignores unknown warning codes is unaffected. An agent that wants the spec hint honoured must omit the flag.

No schema change, no new codes, and the manifest is still accepted and used as written; an agent that reasoned about a page blocked for missing desktop/mobile proof can now read the warning instead of guessing which record was ignored.

changes.summary: The record-shape section no longer says a record that fails one of the three field tests produces no diagnostic; it states that start/prepare-build and doctor warn once per bad record, naming the record, its page_id, and the failing field.

entries.agent_impact: Each entry in polish page-load evidence measurement.warnings[] now carries resource_types[] — the sorted, unique beacon-class resource roles whose failures were demoted to the cross_origin_request_failed warning (drawn from ping, fetch, xhr, other, preflight, so at most five values) — and campaigns-os polish text output prints them as a Resource types: line inside its Capture warnings (not blocking) block. An agent reading a warning can now tell which roles the demotion forgave instead of only which origins failed. The beacon allowlist, the problem codes, measurement.status, the resource ledger and the checkpoint verdict are unchanged: nothing that blocked before warns now, and nothing that warned before blocks. Two consumer-visible consequences: an agent comparing a warning entry against a fixed key set must accept the new key, and page-load evidence recorded before this change whose measurement carries a warning no longer equals the recomputed projection, so evaluateHiddenEagerMediaCheckpoint blocks it as polish.hidden_eager_media.capture_malformed until the route is recaptured.

Evidence with no capture warning, and any evidence captured with this version, needs nothing.

changes.summary: polish text output prints a Resource types: line for each capture warning, filtered to the known resource-type vocabulary.

entries.agent_impact: campaigns-os validate-assembly-report now returns ok:false with the error code stages.assembly.source_package_material_fingerprint when the report declares a Design Source Package material fingerprint (design_source_package.material_fingerprint or an equivalent) but records no stages.assembly.source_package_material_fingerprint. It also returns the error code stages.assembly.waiver_expires_at_invalid for a Source Freshness Waiver record whose expires_at does not parse, which the gate refuses to honor and blocks on as polish.waiver_expires_at_invalid; like the gate, the validator reports only that error for such a report and asks the freshness question once the record is repaired. Both are conditions the polish gate already blocked on, so an agent that validated a hand-authored or hand-patched report and got a clean answer no longer hits a hard stop at doctor or next one command later. A hand-authored report that previously validated may now fail: record the material fingerprint Build consumed, or a structured Source Freshness Waiver in waivers[], exactly as the ladder already required. A report whose Assembly is still pending or that carries no build fingerprint yet is outside the finding, exactly as the gate is not_applicable there, so freshly prepared reports from prepare-build and start still validate. A report with no design source package at all is unaffected, an active waiver still passes, and doctor output is unchanged because doctor keeps reporting this finding from its polish gate and does not list it twice. campaigns-os polish capture is unaffected: its report check stays a shape check, since the polish gate reports source freshness on the way out.

changes.summary: validateAssemblyReport fails a report that declares a design-source-package material fingerprint with no stages.assembly.source_package_material_fingerprint, and one whose source freshness waiver has an unparseable expires_at, reusing the polish gate's predicate and waiver assessment; doctor's shape check and polish capture's report check opt out so the gate's findings are not duplicated or moved earlier.
The freshness-lifecycle section says validate-assembly-report applies the same missing-fingerprint and malformed-waiver conditions as the polish gate.

entries.agent_impact: A `qa run --browser` that a blocked checkpoint, polish, or theme gate finalized before any page was rendered now stamps the verdict with browser: { requested: true, status: "skipped_gate_blocked", blocked_by: [<gate codes>], reason } and prints that reason once on stderr. The reason names the gate and quotes that gate's own required_actions for what clears it, so the guidance matches the exact blocking state (a stale-assembly polish blocker asks for a fresh Build, and a waive command appears only where the gate is waivable). Nothing else moves: the assertion set, the disposition and the exit code (4, blocked) are what they were, and no browser is launched. Treat the field as additive and emitted only for that case — its absence means the verdict makes no claim about a browser pass, not that one ran, so keep reading the browser-runtime assertions and tested_urls to tell whether a browser pass happened. The field is not part of the committed .campaign-runtime/qa-verdict.json allowlist projection, and a --json run receives the stamp in the emitted verdict instead of the stderr line.

changes.summary: The checkpoint-preflight section states the visible downgrade: the browser stamp a gate-blocked --browser run carries, the single stderr line whose repair guidance comes from the gate's required_actions, the unchanged exit code, and that the field's absence is not evidence a browser pass ran.

entries.agent_impact: Credential-bearing requests on the telemetry rails now validate before any socket opens, so two silent behaviours change for an agent. (1) --proxy-base must be https on every rail that carries a credential (Run Telemetry remit, QA verdict publish, telemetry list), not just on telemetry list: a loopback host (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]) is still allowed over plain http and now prints one stderr warning per request that the credential travels in clear, while any other plain-http base — or a base that is not a URL — is refused before the request, so nothing is sent. An agent that pointed a remit or publish at a plain-http remote proxy will see it fail: on the remit rail non-fatally, with the reason in remit_error / remit_ok false; on telemetry list as a non-zero exit. Spec retrieval by --map-id carries no credential and is unaffected. (2) A campaign key that is present but malformed is now reported as refused rather than missing. resolveCampaignsApiKeySource() returns { key, origin, rejected } and describeCampaignKeyRejection() renders a sentence naming the refused SOURCE (env:VAR, the packet field, or the CampaignSpec) and never the value. telemetry list --packet exits non-zero on such a value and makes no request; run-record warns on stderr and its human summary now says the declared key was refused on shape instead of 'no Campaigns API key found', then attempts the send without a tenant scope (the remit rail stays non-fatal); with no send attempted (consent off, or --no-remit) the key is not read and nothing is said about it. A malformed explicit packet value no longer falls through to another source. resolveCampaignsApiKeyValue() keeps its old signature and returns the key or null.
entries.migration: None for https or loopback proxy bases. A plain-http remote --proxy-base now fails on the credential-bearing rails: give that proxy TLS, or run it on a loopback host, or drop the override. If a remit started reporting a refused key, fix the value at the source the warning names (its shape must be 8-256 characters of letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, one line, no whitespace).

changes.summary: telemetry list shares the remit rail's transport gate (https, or loopback over http with an in-clear warning); both telemetry list --packet and run-record now separate a present-but-malformed campaign key from a missing one, naming the refused source and never the value — telemetry list fails fast and makes no request, run-record warns and sends without a tenant scope, and says nothing at all when no send is attempted.
Remit Channel states the credential shape gate and the https/loopback proxy-base rule.
--proxy-base note distinguishes credential-free spec retrieval from the credential-bearing rails and their https/loopback rule.

entries.agent_impact: Text-only change to campaigns-os doctor: the human report now prints a `Required actions:` block listing every checkpoint gate's required_actions[] (one `- [<gate id>] <command or description>` line), below Errors:/Warnings: and above Next:, with `--packet <packet>` substituted for the packet the run read. The gate set is the one `next` aggregates: the registered checkpoint gates plus the polish checkpoint gate. Packet-scoped commands also gain `--report <inspected report>` when the run's Assembly Report is not the packet-inferred default, so the remediation acts on the report the inspection read. A report with no outstanding gate actions prints nothing extra. doctor --json is unchanged in every field, so an agent parsing JSON needs no adaptation; an agent that scrapes the text report can now read the remediation instead of re-running with --json. The lines are produced by the exported doctorRequiredActionLines(result) helper, mirroring nextTinyPromptLines.

changes.summary: Render each checkpoint gate's required_actions[] in the human doctor report as a `Required actions:` block between the findings and the `Next:` block, with the run's packet and its non-default Assembly Report substituted into packet-scoped commands, via a new exported doctorRequiredActionLines(result); JSON output unchanged.
State that the text doctor report prints the same required_actions[] the JSON report carries, under a `Required actions:` block.

entries.agent_impact: Two surface moves in one version. The standardization-report command is removed: it was a second spelling of standardize with identical flags, output and exit codes, and an agent or script still spelling it now gets the unknown-command error pointing at campaigns-os --help. Use standardize; its flags (--target, --family, --slug, --sdk-support-policy, --field-contract, --no-doctor, --json), its output, and the report's own campaign-standardization-report/v0 schema_version are unchanged. entries.agent_impact: New supported CLI command page-kit with one subcommand: campaigns-os page-kit sync --packet <campaign-runtime.build.json> [--dry-run] [--json] writes the CampaignSpec Store Profile fields the spec carries (campaign.store_name, store_url, store_terms, store_privacy, store_contact, store_returns, store_shipping, store_phone, store_phone_tel; NFC-normalized and trimmed as the gate compares them, a target differing only in whitespace or normalization is reported unchanged) into _data/campaigns.json[campaign.public_route_slug] in the packet’s target repo, SEEDS sdk_version (global_config.sdk_version, else the runtime.sdk_version alias, resolved by the same rule the gate uses) while the entry is still in scaffold state or its pin is older than the spec’s and never moves a configured campaign’s pin backwards (not_synced reason target_newer naming both versions; re-save the Map or record the page_kit.sdk_version waiver), prints a field-by-field before -> after diff, and writes nothing else (non-governed keys, other routes, other files untouched; governed fields the spec does not carry are left as they are). The file is edited in place and re-serialized with its own indentation, line ending and trailing newline, staged through a temp file and rename keeping the permission bits, and written only at the path the file resolves to inside the target repo; a round trip that would not reproduce the file byte for byte emits a page_kit.sync.file_reformatted warning. --dry-run prints the diff without writing; --dry-run <value> is an error. Exit 0 on success or a no-op re-run (status synced | dry_run | unchanged); exit 2 with status blocked and nothing written when the packet cannot be read or is not an object (page_kit.sync.packet_invalid), the route slug is absent (route_slug_missing), the spec is absent, unreadable or not an object (spec_missing, spec_invalid), the spec identifies another campaign by spec_identity.public_route_slug (else campaign.slug/id) or spec_identity.map_id (spec_identity_mismatch), the target entry is unavailable (entry_missing with detail.target_status), or the resolved file lies outside the target repo through a symlink (target_escapes_repo). Values the target cannot be made authoritative for are never written and make the status partial (exit 0; doctor will still block): a non-released or conflicting pin (spec_invalid | spec_conflict), a field of the wrong type (spec_invalid_type), a URL field that is not an http(s) URL (not_http_url), a store_phone_tel that is not a tel: URI (not_tel_uri), control characters (control_characters), the demo value itself in the spec (demo_residue), and demo residue in a field the spec does not carry (demo_residue_not_in_spec); each lands in not_synced[] with its reason and a page_kit.sync.<field>_not_synced warning; store_contact may also be a mailto: address. A gate under an active named-human checkpoint waiver is not reversed: its fields land in not_synced[] with reason waived naming waived_by and the target stays as the waiver accepted it; sync reads the Assembly Report doctor would (Build Context binding, default sidecar, or --report <path>; unreadable is a page_kit.sync.report_unreadable warning). Unknown flags are rejected (known: --packet, --dry-run, --json, --report). When the report records a terminal build, a page_kit.sync.build_stale warning says _site/ was rendered from the old entry and next points at the rebuild. A write marks the retained doctor sidecar stale (failure to do so is a page_kit.sync.doctor_sidecar_not_marked warning). --json emits { ok, action: "page-kit sync", status, packet_path, public_route_slug, target_repo, target_path, campaigns_path, spec_path, dry_run, written, changes[] { field, before, after, source }, unchanged[], not_in_spec[], not_synced[] { field, reason, detail }, errors[], warnings[], next }. Doctor and next: the repair_target required action of the page_kit.store_profile and page_kit.sdk_version gates is now kind command with command "campaigns-os page-kit sync --packet <packet>" (was kind edit, command null) wherever the target can be made authoritative from a usable spec value — sdk_version target_missing, target_invalid and a mismatch sync would write (target behind the spec, or scaffold state; a configured campaign whose pin is newer than the spec’s keeps an edit action); store_profile demo_residue, target_missing, mismatch, target_invalid_type with a present, well-shaped, non-demo spec value — so doctor’s Required actions block, next’s next_actions[] at doctor-blocked (ids checkpoint.page_kit.store_profile.repair_target and checkpoint.page_kit.sdk_version.repair_target) and emitted required_actions[].command print the pasteable command with the real packet path, spelled for the running install (npx campaigns-os page-kit sync … from a consumer install); any other store_profile blocker keeps an edit action naming the spec field and reason (spec_invalid_type, not_http_url, not_tel_uri, control_characters, demo_residue, missing). next’s doctor-blocked checkpoint actions are now spelled through the install prefix like every other printed command. The QA runner’s browser-skipped notice renders gate actions through the same install-prefix rule as doctor and next (the --packet <packet> placeholder stays; the verdict never carries a local path). The command is not pipeline-advancing and never records a deviation. contracts/supported-surface.json cli_commands gains page-kit and surface_version moves 1.28.0 -> 1.29.0; docs/supported-surface.md, docs/build-packet.md (Store Profile and SDK-version checkpoints), the README and docs/quickstart.md first-verdict paragraphs, and the regenerated orientation reference and runtime-readiness guide name the command. entries.agent_impact: The Assembly Report's top-level status, next and blockers are now derived from stages on every write (prepare-build's first write and every stage record or operator edit after it) instead of written once by prepare-build. status reads blocked while any recorded stage is blocked, completed only once every recorded stage (prepare_build and doctor included, not just the ladder) is terminal, and prepared otherwise, so a prepare-build --no-doctor report never reads completed; before this a finished ladder still read status prepared, next.stage setup and blockers [] beside a stages.qa of completed_with_warnings or blocked. blockers is the union of the blockers[] of the stages currently blocked. next uses the next <stage> vocabulary: next.stage is the first non-terminal ladder stage (setup, build, polish, deploy, qa, done) or prepare-build / doctor-blocked when that gate is blocked, or doctor when the ladder is exhausted but doctor never recorded an outcome, next.owner is the owning skill, and next.blocked true marks the stage holding the ladder. A consumer that branched on next.stage === 'assembly' must branch on 'build', on 'collect-inputs' on 'prepare-build', and one that expected status 'prepared' for a finished campaign must accept 'completed'. next and doctor no longer treat a terminal stages.prepare_build beside status blocked as a contradiction when another stage is the one blocked. A report written before this change is rewritten once on its next commit; an unchanged re-record still leaves the file's bytes alone. The report schema is unchanged (status is a free string, next keeps stage/owner/action). commitAssemblyReport (src/stage-ledger.mjs, internal) throws a TypeError when a mutator returns a non-object other than null/undefined.

entries.agent_impact: stages.assembly.build_fingerprint has a defined algorithm and doctor computes it. Build copies derived.build_output_fingerprint.value onto stages.assembly.build_fingerprint after page-kit build instead of typing a value; the build prompt says so. The polish gate (doctor derived.polish_gate, QA's polish assertion) now compares evidence against the recomputed output value: a drifted output is the new gate code polish.output_drift with current_output_fingerprint set and required_actions [rerun_build, run_polish], even when source_build_fingerprint equals the recorded string (polish.stale stays the code for evidence stamped against an older recorded build). polish capture refuses by name when the built route root is missing, when the output cannot be read (EACCES and the like are caught and named, never thrown raw), or when the output drifted, and its binding carries assembly.output_fingerprint. Symbolic links inside _site/ are skipped, never hashed or followed. A consumer that stamped a placeholder sha256 string onto stages.assembly.build_fingerprint over a real built _site/ now sees built_output.fingerprint_stale; record the doctor-published value. entries.agent_impact: The typed-card runner (qa run --test-order) loads the checkout once per order path instead of twice. The entered_via_landing step's selector probe is the checkout's only load on a path: when the probe finds a selection surface, opened_checkout records detail "already on checkout from the selector probe; not re-opened" (previously no detail) rather than loading the same URL again; on a landing-entry family the probe load is followed only by the landing page and the SDK's own navigation. A multi-path plan (tiers:*, several coupons) probes each checkout URL once per run and reuses the answer on later paths; entered_via_landing evidence gains selection_surface_probe: "loaded" on the path that ran the probe and "reused" on the rest ("failed" plus selection_surface_probe_error when the page-side read broke; that path proceeds to the entry page as before and the failure is never reused), and a reused skip detail ends with "(probe answer reused from an earlier path of this run)". A reused answer on a selector family opens the checkout once in opened_checkout (detail null, as before); on a landing-entry family the path goes straight to the landing page. A consumer counting SDK page-view events in the analytics-correctness or receipt capture will see one checkout view per path where it saw two; one matching opened_checkout.detail === null on selector families must accept the new detail string. Step names, statuses, order and failure codes are unchanged. No schema, flag or command change.

entries.agent_impact: Browser QA's template-residue:<page>:payment-chrome:<method> assertion now decides untouched-vs-edited for a referenced .svg by hashing the served bytes against the shipped starter hash the shared-commerce brand contract records (default_residue.payment_chrome.asset_sha256, pinned by asset_pin.sha), not by whether the SVG markup names the method. An unmodified starter asset (the shipped upsell-payment-logos.svg names no method in its markup) is residue: status fail at the residue severity, actual "residue found: <basename> [starter], <other assets>, <visible selectors>" (starter assets first, tagged inline), and a new evidence.starter_assets[] listing the hash-matched basenames beside referenced_assets[] and edited_assets[]. The digest is over the raw served bytes. Before, that asset produced status manual_review with actual "edited in place: ... no longer carries <method> chrome" on a page that had never been polished. Different bytes that no longer name the method are still manual_review with the unchanged edited-in-place line; different bytes that still name the method, and any asset that cannot be read (raster, 404, timed-out or oversized read), are still residue. Loading a brand contract whose payment_chrome.assets[] lists an asset with no asset_sha256 entry, or a malformed one, now throws (code payment_chrome_hash_missing / payment_chrome_hash_invalid, naming the asset); a contract with no asset_sha256 map at all still loads and uses the markup test. An agent that read manual_review on this assertion as "the operator already removed the marks" must now expect fail on an untouched starter strip and dispatch the removal; evidence.starter_assets says which basenames were byte-identical to the starter. No command, flag or schema change; the brand contract gains two optional fields (asset_sha256, asset_pin) that nothing on the supported surface names.

entries.agent_impact: New supported CLI command spec with one subcommand: campaigns-os spec derive --packet <campaign-runtime.build.json> [--dry-run] [--json] [--report <json>] writes the repo-derived CampaignSpec fields (#432 field classes: authored | mirrored | derived) into the packet’s local spec (spec.local_path) from the target repo alone, no network: global_config.sdk_version (and the runtime.sdk_version alias when declared) from _data/campaigns.json[public_route_slug].sdk_version; each active page’s page_url from the page tree under assembly.output_dir (default src/<slug>/) by page-kit’s own rule: the file’s basename alone (a nested index.html is not read), or a frontmatter permalink in the /<slug>/<route>/ form prepare-build writes (any other spelling is target_invalid naming the served URL; false/null/~, trailing comments and a BOM read as page-kit reads them); the legacy funnel_pages[].page_url mirror is reconciled every run, bound by the packet’s source_html.pages[].page_kit.target_path first, else by route, terminal segment or filename; analytics.providers.gtm.containerId from gtm_id and analytics.providers.facebook.pixelId from fb_pixel_id (provider blocks created as { enabled: true, … } when absent). Prints a field-by-field before -> after diff with each value’s repo source; overwrites an authored-looking value in a derived field (the diff shows it); writes nothing else (store profile is slice 2). Status derived | dry_run | unchanged | partial (exit 0), partial when a field lands in not_derived[] with reason scaffold_seed (entry still carries the starter demo store profile; page-kit sync seeds the pin the other way), target_missing, target_invalid, waived (active page_kit.sdk_version waiver, spec left as accepted), page_tree_missing, page_file_not_found, page_file_ambiguous, waivers_unknown (Assembly Report unreadable; the pin waits), page_id_duplicate, entry_route_undeclared (index.html binds a page not flagged is_entry), spec_container_invalid (a spec container of the wrong type, reported by the plan so dry-run and write agree), spec_ahead (the spec pin is ahead of the repo pin: doctor’s blocked state, page-kit sync’s repair; derive never moves a spec pin backwards), or target_empty (an empty repo id never deletes a spec id); a placeholder id (GTM-XXXXXXX, a run of one digit) is target_invalid; not_in_target[] lists derived fields the entry does not carry. Routes are compared the way prepare-build projects them (normalized, slug prefix stripped). After a write the Build Context spec.hash/material_hash and the Assembly Report identity.spec_hash/spec_material_hash are re-bound to the new spec when they were bound to the replaced one and name that spec file (another packet’s sidecar is never re-bound) (rebound { build_context, assembly_report } on the result; QA and bundle check correlate on the material hash). Warnings: spec.derive.routing_hint_stale (a standing check: an sdk_hints.meta_tags routing hint no longer matches the derived route of the page it names; hints are not rewritten), spec.derive.projection_stale (a route moved; the packet’s page-kit projection and Build Context page map were prepared from the old routes; re-run prepare-build), spec.derive.identity_not_rebound (a sidecar already carried another spec identity and was left alone), spec.derive.analytics_block_created (a provider block was created from the repo id, so QA gates on it); --dry-run carries the file_reformatted / projection_stale / build_stale warnings phrased as what a write would do; spec.derive.file_reformatted, spec.derive.build_stale, spec.derive.report_unreadable, spec.derive.doctor_sidecar_not_marked. Write discipline as page-kit sync: one read, in-place edit keeping indent/EOL/trailing newline, temp file created with the spec’s mode bits + rename after re-reading the spec (spec.derive.spec_changed_underneath, exit 2, when it changed since the read), written only where the spec resolves inside its own directory or the target repo (spec.derive.spec_escapes_boundary), doctor sidecar marked stale after a write; --dry-run writes nothing; unknown flags and a valued --dry-run are rejected. Exit 2 with status blocked, a spec.derive.* error (packet_invalid, route_slug_missing, spec_missing, spec_invalid, spec_identity_mismatch, entry_missing with detail.target_status, page_tree_unreadable, write_failed, spec_changed_underneath) and nothing written; a bare --report is rejected. --json emits { ok, action: "spec derive", status, packet_path, public_route_slug, target_repo, campaigns_path, page_tree, spec_path, report_path, dry_run, written, changes[] { field, path, before, after, source, page_id? }, unchanged[], not_derived[] { field, reason, detail, page_id? }, not_in_target[], stale_hints[], rebound { build_context, assembly_report }, errors[], warnings[], next }. Not pipeline-advancing, never records a deviation. entries.agent_impact: Facts about the lifecycle journal, however the journal was selected (--lifecycle-journal, CAMPAIGNS_OS_LIFECYCLE_LOG, or an active run session). A known command run with --no-write no longer appends an entry. A refused invocation — an unknown command, an unknown subcommand refused before its handler runs, or a flag the command refuses up front — never appends one and creates no file of its own, with or without --no-write. A command that fails inside its handler still appends; `next <unknown-stage>` is such a failure, because it resolves the workspace before it rejects the stage. `run status` never appends one, with or without --no-write. One effect still precedes argument refusal: `start`, `prepare-build`, `build`, `run start` and `run end` close out a stale run session at the root they are about to act on (Run Record assembled and remitted under the usual consent, session file cleared) before argv is refused — a declared effect of those commands, now suppressed by --no-write, which therefore leaves the target byte-identical. A workflow that needs a journal entry for an inspection must run a known command without --no-write; removing --no-write from a refused invocation or from `run status` will not produce one. A workflow that relied on `run end --no-write` reporting a stale closeout gets "no active run session to end" instead: --no-write no longer performs the closeout it could not record.

entries.agent_impact: A new supported CLI command, `campaigns-os readback <target-repo-root> [--json]`, projects a read-only view of a run's emitted artifacts and writes nothing under the target (no lifecycle journal entry either). Its JSON payload is the new `campaigns-os-readback/v2` contract: staleness is assessed per artifact, so `staleness.stale` is true when ANY loaded artifact predates the checkout's last HEAD movement, where the previous projection compared only the newest artifact and reported such a set fresh. A consumer gating on freshness should accept `campaigns-os-readback/v2` and read `staleness.stale_keys` or `staleness.artifacts` to name the stale artifacts. An artifact that recorded a `generated_at` the readback cannot parse has an age it never established: `staleness.unparseable_keys` names those artifacts in render order, their artifact rows carry the shape of the refused value rather than the value, and `clean` is false whenever that list is non-empty, so an unknown age can no longer ride along on a fresh sibling. `computable` and `stale` keep their meanings, and an artifact carrying no `generated_at` key at all is unchanged — it recorded no age to check, so it stays out of the comparison and is not by itself unclean. Separately, the four mutating commands that lacked one gain `--dry-run`: `run-record`, `qa publish`, `checkpoint waive` and `theme waive`. Each validates and assembles exactly as the real command does, writes nothing under the target and opens no connection, and exits as the real command would — so an agent can preview a Run Record, a verdict publish or a waiver before committing to it. Validation is not weaker under the flag: every check on the route from argv to the first effect runs, by the same code, including the ones that live inside the effect — an invalid Run Record is refused with the writer's own message and exit 1, a waive over a report that is not an Assembly Report object is refused as the commit refuses it, and a `--proxy-base` the transport declines before it opens a socket fails `qa publish --dry-run` with `publish_failed` and exit 1 exactly as the real publish does. The envelopes gain `dry_run: true` plus `would_write`/`would_remit` and `would_remit_refused` (run-record), `would_publish`/`would_post` with `status: "dry_run"` (qa publish), and `would_write` with `status: "dry_run"` (both waives); `run end` carries the flag through and leaves the session open. On those commands a `--dry-run` invocation also appends no command-lifecycle entry and runs no stale-session closeout, so an idle session is left on disk for a real invocation and `run end --dry-run` at a root whose only session is stale refuses with `No active run session to end`; on a command that does not implement the flag (`qa run`, say) the shared parser still accepts it and the command behaves exactly as before, lifecycle entry included. No existing command, flag or output changed.
